newsitem.title: FRANCE: Serbian opposition ponders Milosevic backtrack.
newsitem.headline: Serbian opposition ponders Milosevic backtrack.

text.p: Serbian opposition leaders met France's foreign minister on Thursday as they considered their response to President Slobodan Milosevic's decision to reinstate their election wins after prolonged street protests.

The leaders of the three-party Together, or Zajedno, democratic opposition coalition met Foreign Minister Herve de Charette and were due to give a news conference at 12.30 p.m. (1130 GMT), officials said.

Milosevic, in a concession to pro-democracy demonstrators, said on Wednesday he wanted parliament to approve special legislation reinstating the disputed results of elections in 14 cities and towns including Belgrade. The Tanjug news agency said Milosevic's government had approved a draft law which parliament would consider in extraordinary session on Tuesday.

De Charette, meeting opposition leaders Zoran Djindjic, Vuk Draskovic and Vesna Pesic, has cautiously hailed Milosevic's move as a step in the right direction but expressed hope it was not simply a delaying tactic.
Opposition groups have said that protests should continue until their demands are met in full. A march in Belgrade was scheduled for Thusday evening after the opposition leaders returned from Paris.
Apart from recognition of the election victories, Milosevic's opponents want to free media from state control and set up an independent judiciary.
The Paris talks are a symbolic way of stepping up the pressure on Milosevic. France said it was recognising the opposition coalition by inviting its leaders to Paris.
The Zajedno coalition, students and professional groups, from laywers to actors, have braved police baton charges to demand democratic reforms with rallies of tens of thousands of people.
